scenes.headline: How an adapter turns an image editor into an outpainter
scenes.sub: Pad the picture with gray, and keep it exactly where it was.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Mothball! Qwen Image two point one edits pictures, but cannot extend one. A small adapter changes that.

scenes.text: Pad the picture with flat gray, and train the editor that gray means unknown and everything else means keep it exactly here.
scenes.say: The idea: flat gray means unknown. Everything else means keep it exactly where it is.

steps.say: The padded canvas is compressed into clean condition tokens, at noise level zero.
The target starts as pure noise, on the same grid, and runs through thirty-two blocks.

steps.note: the target reads the condition; never the reverse
steps.say: At every block the target can read the condition. The condition never reads the target.
But nothing pins the known pixels. Without the adapter, the model sometimes moves them.

scenes.title: Two older ways, and this one

left.title: Mask channel or blending
left.say: Older methods either get a mask channel, or overwrite the known region at every step.

right.title: This adapter
items: The mask is the gray itself
right.say: This one gets neither. The gray is the mask, and keeping the picture is learned.

scenes.title: Why the paste-back seam shows
scenes.say: Workflows paste the original back at the end. That only works if the picture stayed in place.

parts.note: a shift: the same size everywhere
parts.say: A shift breaks every line that crosses the seam.

parts.note: a rescale: worst at the corners
parts.say: A rescale is invisible at the centre and worst at the corners.

steps.say: Without the adapter, Qwen rescaled her, and the pasted original made a second person.
With version two, she stays in place and the stitch disappears.

scenes.title: Kept area against the original, on four CPU cores
scenes.note: one NASA photo, one seed, 8 steps
scenes.say: I ran it on four CPU cores. Without the adapter, the scene moved twenty-eight pixels. With it, the picture stayed put, to the pixel.

scenes.label: of the canvas kept, in version two's training data
scenes.say: Forty-five to ninety-three percent is how much of the canvas version two trained on keeping. Not a promise.

scenes.text: Gray means unknown; everything else stays exactly where it was. Registration is what makes the stitch invisible.
scenes.say: Gray means unknown. Everything else stays exactly where it was, and that is what makes the stitch invisible.

recap: The canvas is a clean prefix
The adapter learns to keep them
scenes.say: The canvas is a clean prefix. Nothing pins the known pixels. The adapter learns to keep them.
